subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in inbound WhatsApp Baileys call-event tracking, and which sanitized surface should expose that activity to agents?
rationale: The missing listener is clear, but call metadata affects privacy, access control, retention, and contact-activity semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent behavior contract.

options.title: Approve opt-in plugin tracking
options.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp plugin listener for Baileys call events, filter it like inbound messages, and expose one documented sanitized activity surface.

options.title: Design the surface first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide between plugin hooks, session metadata, contact activity storage, or a query/tool API.

options.title: Decline inbound call tracking
options.body: Close the direction if OpenClaw should avoid storing or exposing WhatsApp call metadata even when Baileys emits it.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in plugin tracking
recommendation.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp plugin listener for Baileys call events, filter it like inbound messages, and expose one documented sanitized activity surface.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent WhatsApp call-related history and already scoped this as WhatsApp-plugin-owned work in the issue discussion.
